text:
maria (AE): Quick checklist request from Acme post-POC: they want all access removed and a confirmation of what data we're keeping.
chris (Solutions Eng): Minimal sweep we've used before:
- Hosted API keys revoked
- Drain + deprovision Dedicated pools
- Revoke service accounts / rotate creds
- Remove VPC peering and firewall rules (if we managed them)
- Confirm deletion or legal hold for logs and buckets
maria (AE): Who picks these up internally? Need an ETA to tell the customer.
irene (Infra): I can take Dedicated pool teardown and bucket sweep. Need a ticket and legal approval if they want any hold applied. I can do the work in a 2-hour maintenance window.
sam (Sales-Engineer): Hosted keys: if they used long-lived keys we rotate then expire old key after 24h. If ephemeral keys were used for the demo, revoke immediately.
devops-bot: Revoke command for hosted keys:
```
redwood-cli keys revoke --org acme-corp --key-id <KEY_ID>
# verify: redwood-cli keys list --org acme-corp
```
chris (Solutions Eng): Dedicated pool teardown process: 1) set pool to drain 2) allow existing inferences to finish (or force-stop after 10m) 3) snapshot metrics/KV cache if requested 4) decommission GPUs and delete pool config
maria (AE): Acme mentioned they may require 7-year retention for some access logs. Who signs off on that?
anne (Legal): We need a written request from their security contact. For >90 days retention we either export to their S3 (preferred) or open a legal hold. If legal hold, include exact retention window and copy me on the ticket.
maria (AE): I'll ask them for the security contact and the retention spec.
sam (Sales-Engineer): Note: Dedicated pools sometimes create ephemeral snapshot objects. Our cleanup preserves poc-* prefixes for 30 days by default. Irene, can that be overridden with approval?
irene (Infra): Yes, default is 30 days. If they confirm no legal hold I can run an immediate sweep. Command I use:
```
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-prod-assets --recursive --exclude "*" --include "poc-acme-*"
```
anne (Legal): Before deletion, export access logs and a checksum manifest to our secure archive and attach to the ticket.
maria (AE): Proposed timeline: once Acme confirms no legal hold, we revoke hosted keys and sweep buckets same day; Dedicated drain + teardown within 48 hours. Good?
chris (Solutions Eng): Sounds good. Also if they used Private (VPC) deployment: we cannot delete customer-managed peering or routes. Their infra team must remove peering and confirm.
maria (AE): I'll make sure to tell them.
ben (Support): For audits I'll attach a post-POC closure pack to the account including: key revocation logs, pool teardown job IDs, S3 deletion manifest, exported logs (if retained), and ticket numbers.
maria (AE): Thanks. One last thing: paste the exact list I should send to the customer for sign-off so I can DM and cc legal.
chris (Solutions Eng): Send them:
- Confirm: no legal hold on logs/objects (or provide written hold request)
- Hosted API keys: will be revoked immediately (include client rotation plan)
- Dedicated pools: drain then teardown (48h) - indicate any artifacts to snapshot
- Private/VPC: customer must remove peering and share confirmation
- Data retention: specify export destination (S3 path) for >90 days
- Final: we will provide deletion manifests and audit logs when complete
maria (AE): Perfect, I'll send that now and loop back once they reply :pray:
